Agentic workflows operate in a project workspace, reading and writing
across the same files, pipelines, notes, and references a researcher uses.
Their effectiveness on any given project depends heavily on the structure
of that workspace.

When a project follows mature conventions, an agent navigates it with
little prompting and writes its output back into the same structured form.
The conventions do most of the work.

\itshape Each of these tools is mature in its own right. Together they form a \textbf{project surface} an agent can read and write across without leaving the repository.
\end{center}

## What the agent works with

Four structured pieces a project exposes when organized this way.

- **Memory.** A structured set of project notes (ideas, tasks, results,
  meeting records, decisions on disk) sitting next to an activity log of
  every tool call. The reasoning behind any later claim is reconstructible
  by reading the project's git history.
- **Grounding in literature and existing code.** A curated project
  bibliography and a catalog of code libraries (project plus external
  mirrors) that the agent consults while writing. Claims get linked
  to citations as they appear; new code builds on existing libraries.
- **Exploratory power and rerunnable pipelines.** Interactive notebooks,
  for example marimo with HoloViews/Bokeh. The agent can author and edit
  these notebooks alongside the researcher in real time. Once the
  researcher decides to apply the method across the database, the agent
  can be prompted to promote the program into a pipeline (Snakemake with
  config files).
- **Communication.** Quarto reports, revealjs slide decks, and eventually manuscript
  sections all re-render from the same data, pipelines, and bibliography.
  The same project tree, including reports, can be published as a GitHub or GitLab Pages site
  that an agent keeps up to date for collaborators.

## Still brittle

- Agents produce structure faster than researchers can maintain it.
- Context retrieval still needs human checking.

\begin{center}
\itshape Open-science structure makes a project legible to agents. The researcher stays in charge of the research.
\end{center}
